In this article LCID Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Brand new Lucid electric cars sit parked in front of a Lucid Studio showroom in San Francisco on May 24, 2024. Justin Sullivan | Getty Images Lucid Group reported a 6.7% decrease in year-over-year vehicle deliveries during the third quarter, after the embattled all-electric vehicle maker cut production to better align with slower customer demand. The U.S. automaker, which is heavily backed by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, on Monday said it delivered 3,806 EVs and produced 2,954 vehicles from July through September. Those results compare with deliveries of 4,078 EVs on production of 3,891 vehicles in the year-ago quarter. Deliveries of Lucid vehicles are 3.4% higher through the third quarter than a year earlier. Production has climbed 33%, as Lucid ramped up vehicle production through early this year. Lucid's highest quarterly production of nearly 7,900 units occurred during the fourth quarter of last year, followed by 5,500 during the first quarter of this year. Shares of Lucid closed up less than 1% on Monday at $4.17 and were little changed in extended trading following the delivery data. The turnaround plan includes identifying $1.4 billion in cash flow improvement opportunities this year. They include approximately $600 million to $800 million in vehicle inventory, $500 million in capital expenditures, and $200 million in operating expenses, the company said when reporting its second-quarter results in August. headlines.article_text: SpaceX stock climbs highest since June, returning Musk to trillionaire Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points SpaceX shares rose almost 8% on Monday, lifting CEO Elon Musk back to trillionaire status. Last week, SpaceX successfully launched a crewed NASA mission, and separately sent Google's AI chips into orbit. The stock has rebounded since bottoming in August. In this article SPCX Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Elon Musk, chief executive officer of Tesla Inc., during a state dinner with Chinese President Xi Jinping, not pictured, in the East Room of the White House in Washington, DC, US, on Thursday, Sept. 24, 2026. Annabelle Gordon | Bloomberg | Getty Images SpaceX shares rose almost 8% on Monday, reaching their highest since mid-June, shortly after Elon Musk's company held its record initial public offering . With the rally, Musk is once again a trillionaire. The jump followed a Sunday note from Morgan Stanley analysts, who called SpaceX "cheap" at today's prices, and highlighted "future AI product releases, Starship progress, and additional neocloud contracts." They recommend buying the stock and have a $300 price target, representing an increase of about 75% from Monday's $171.09 close. Late last week SpaceX conducted multiple historic flights in a single day, including sending a crewed mission for NASA to the International Space Station, and a separate launch of Google AI chips into orbit. The Morgan Stanley analysts suggested investors buy SpaceX shares before the company's next planned test flight for its massive Starship rocket, and ahead of its third-quarter earnings report expected in late October. Starship is SpaceX's next-generation spacecraft, the largest rocket ever built, and is designed to be fully reusable with both its upper stage and booster able to land safely back on Earth. The system is expected to supercharge SpaceX's business, bringing the company's Starlink satellites into orbit, as well as cargo and crews from other companies and agencies. Should SpaceX attempt a Starship upper stage ship catch in its next test flight, that could be "the biggest positive catalyst since the IPO," the analysts wrote. In prior test flights, the Starship upper stage has made splash downs in the ocean, but hasn't been proven reusable. SpaceX is also getting a boost from its artificial intelligence business, which it gained through the acquisition of Musk's xAI last year and expanded through the recent acquisition of Cursor. While the company's homegrown Grok model hasn't taken off compared to leading models from OpenAI and Anthropic, SpaceX is generating hefty revenue by renting out capacity to the likes of Google and Anthropic. Musk has the benefit of close ties to the Trump administration. On Wednesday, the Pentagon appointed Musk as co-lead of Project Meridian , an initiative that involves identifying weapons, technologies and military capabilities the U.S. may need in future wars. SpaceX makes a large chunk of its revenue from the U.S. government and increasingly from defense contracts, earning over $12.7 billion to date from its work with the Defense Department, according to FedScout. Musk said over the weekend he will be renaming SpaceX's AI division, known as SpaceXAI, as SpaceXSI, embracing President Donald Trump's new branding. As his company's stock soared on Monday, Musk was notably absent from a New York City Council hearing , where city officials grilled AI leaders and researchers about how the technology should be regulated. Representatives from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta were in attendance to testify. Councilmember Shekar Krishnan noted, "AI has taken over our economy, inflated valuations, stealing our public land for data centers, and increasing the net worth of AI CEOs like Elon Musk, who became our first ever trillionaire." According to Forbes' real-time billionaires list , Musk is currently worth $1.03 trillion, factoring in his holdings in Tesla and SpaceX. SpaceX went public on June 12, and jumped to a record close of $201.80 on June 16. The shares started trending lower soon thereafter, bottoming in early August. They've since climbed about 58%. SpaceX didn't immediately respond to a request for comment. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing , SpaceX — Elon Musk confirmed discussions with TSMC about helping his Terafab chip venture operate its Texas factories. Shares of Intel, which is also participating in the Terafab project, slid about 2%. TSM's stock climbed 2%, and shares of SpaceX jumped 6%. Sphere Entertainment — Shares tumbled 12% after Craig-Hallum Capital downgraded shares to hold from buy, per StreetAccount. The company pointed to demand for "The Wizard of Oz" softening faster than anticipated, which could put estimates for the second half of 2026 and first half of 2027 at risk. Vaxcyte — Shares jumped about 30% after the biotech company announced positive top-line results from the Phase 3 trial of its pneumococcal conjugate vaccine in adults aged 50 and over. The immune responses were comparable to those of Pfizer's Prevnar 20 and Merck's Capvaxive. Millrose Properties , Lennar — Shares of both companies fell roughly 6%. On Friday, Hunterbrook Media ran a short report calling into question the economics of Millrose's single-family rental investments and Lennar's potential influence over the company's strategy. Microsoft — The software giant jumped more than 1% on the back of an upgrade to buy from Melius Research. Analyst Ben Reitzes said that the company has an edge in artificial intelligence as security becomes a focal point. "[Microsoft CEO] Satya Nadella and his team are increasingly going to be considered the 'adults in charge' — a key cog in the security, governance and the 'AI CYA' play that is likely in the early innings," he wrote. Brazilian stocks — The group rallied after right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro finished ahead of incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva by around 2 percentage points in election's first round held Sunday. The iShares MSCI Brazil ETF (EWZ) surged 13%. U.S.-listed shares of Itau Unibanco and Banco Bradesco soared 16% and 19%, respectively. Shares of Mercado Libre , which deems Brazil to be one of its major markets , advanced 8%. PTC — Shares surged 33% after the software company agreed to be acquired by Schneider Electric for $205 per share, valuing the company's equity at more than $22 billion. The transaction is expected to close by the third quarter of 2027. Wells Fargo — Shares gained 1% after a Morgan Stanley upgrade to overweight from equal weight . "Normalizing balance sheet growth should ease funding pressure, stabilize [net interest margin], and raises our conviction in the path to higher returns," analyst Manan Gosalia said in a note. DraftKings — Shares of the digital sports entertainment and gaming company popped over 7% after a Bank of America upgrade to buy from neutral. Bank of America's Julie Hoover said the company's prediction markets are a "win-win," expecting prediction markets can generate $400 million in fees for 2027 and between $200 million to $400 million in market making. Estee Lauder — The beauty stock moved 2% higher on the back of an upgrade at Barclays to overweight from equal weight. The bank said it is bullish on Estée Lauder's growth and earnings profile over the next several years. Harley-Davidson —The motorcycle builder's stock rose about 10% after an upgrade to buy from neutral at Citi. Going from a "modest" retail improvement earlier this year, Citi believes the motorcycle company will benefit from a major product introduction, cost savings and potential earnings tail winds from LiveWire. — CNBC's Nick Wells, Michelle Fox, Ananya Chetia and Paulina Likos contributed reporting.
